conventional_description: Genital herpes is a common sexually transmitted infection caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV), usually type 2 but sometimes type 1. After initial infection, the virus travels to nerve cells near the spine and stays there for life, periodically reactivating to cause outbreaks. Typical symptoms include clusters of small, painful blisters or sores on the genitals or surrounding skin, often with itching, burning, or tingling before they appear. Diagnosis is usually made by physical exam, swab test, or blood test for antibodies. While not life-threatening, it can cause significant physical discomfort and emotional distress.
conventional_treatments: Standard treatment focuses on antiviral medications like acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir, taken either episodically at the first sign of an outbreak or daily as suppressive therapy to reduce frequency. Over-the-counter pain relievers, cool compresses, and keeping the area clean and dry are also recommended. These drugs can shorten healing time and lessen severity but do not eliminate the virus from the body.
tcm_understanding:
In TCM, genital herpes is seen as a manifestation of pathogenic factors that have invaded the body's lower burner, particularly the Liver channel, which runs through the genitals. The most common acute outbreaks arise from Damp-Heat or Toxic-Heat-think of it as a combination of moisture and heat that becomes trapped and inflamed, producing the classic burning blisters. When the body's cooling and moistening reserves (Yin) are low, a different kind of heat, called empty heat, can flare up, causing milder but recurrent sores.
But the story doesn't end with heat. If the body's vital energy (Qi) and blood are deficient, the immune response is too weak to contain the virus, leading to chronic, slow-healing lesions. And in some cases, when internal warmth is lacking, cold and dampness congeal in the lower body, creating hard, dark sores that ache dully rather than burn. This is why two people with the same Western diagnosis may need completely opposite treatments-one might require cooling, detoxifying herbs, while another needs warming, strengthening formulas.
The key is that TCM identifies the specific pattern behind your outbreaks by looking at the sores themselves (their color, pain, discharge) and your overall picture (tongue, pulse, energy, digestion). This pattern diagnosis guides treatment not just to heal the current episode but to alter the internal environment so future outbreaks become less frequent and less intense.
classical_quote: 「阴疮者，由三阴经热毒不散，或房室不洁，邪气交争，发于阴器，故生疮。」
classical_translation: "Genital sores arise when heat toxins from the three Yin channels fail to dissipate, or when unclean sexual activity causes pathogenic Qi to struggle in the genital area, resulting in ulceration."
classical_source:
Zhu Bing Yuan Hou Lun (Treatise on the Origins and Symptoms of Diseases)  ,  Volume 40, 'Yin Chuang Hou' (Genital Sores) 									·

tcm_diagnosis:
When a practitioner sees an acute outbreak with clusters of clear blisters that quickly become painful, burning sores with sticky yellow discharge, they suspect Damp-Heat in the Liver Channel. The tongue is red with a greasy yellow coating, and the pulse is wiry and rapid. Because the Liver Channel runs through the genital area, this pattern is the most common culprit behind first or severe episodes.
If the same heat and damp intensify, they can transform into Toxic-Heat. Here the local redness and swelling are extreme, pustules may form, and the whole body reacts with fever and thirst. The tongue is deep red with a thick yellow coat, and the pulse is forceful and rapid. This is a more aggressive flare that needs stronger clearing and detoxifying action.
Recurrent outbreaks that are milder - maybe just a few small blisters or a tingling sensation - often point to Empty-Heat from Yin Deficiency. The person may feel hot flushes, night sweats, and a dry mouth, especially in the evening. The tongue is red with little or no coating, and the pulse is thin and rapid. This pattern flares when the body's cooling reserves are low.
When outbreaks are chronic and sores heal slowly, the underlying issue may be Qi and Blood Deficiency. The skin is pale, the person feels tired and weak, and the sores linger rather than erupting violently. The tongue is pale with a thin white coat, and the pulse is weak or thready. This pattern reflects a lack of resources to repair and defend the tissues.
Less commonly, a practitioner encounters hard, dark lumps that ache dully and suppurate slowly, without the redness and heat of the previous patterns. This is Cold-Dampness congealing in the lower burner. The person often has cold hands and feet, a pale tongue with a white greasy coating, and a deep, slow pulse. It requires warming and dispersing treatment.

patterns.symptoms: ["Burning genital pain", "Clustered blisters with sticky yellow discharge", "Bitter taste in the mouth", "Dark, scanty urine", "Heaviness in the lower body", "Rib-side fullness or discomfort"]
patterns.worse_with: Spicy, greasy, or fried foods, Alcohol, Emotional stress, anger, or worry, Hot, humid weather, Overwork and fatigue
patterns.better_with: Cooling foods and drinks, Keeping genitals clean and dry, Gentle exercise, Stress reduction, Cool environment
patterns.why_this_happens: The Liver channel runs through the genitals. When Damp-Heat accumulates in the Liver and Gallbladder, it surges downward along this pathway, causing acute outbreaks of clustered blisters with burning pain and sticky yellow discharge. The Heat component creates redness and intense burning, while the Dampness leads to swelling, oozing, and a heavy sensation. This combination is the classic presentation of a Damp-Heat genital herpes flare.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with redder sides, yellow greasy coating thicker at the centre and root. Pulse: wiry, slippery, and rapid, especially wiry at the left Guan position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Spicy, greasy, and fried foods generate Damp-Heat internally, while alcohol directly adds Heat and aggravates the Liver. Emotional stress and anger cause Liver Qi stagnation, which can transform into Fire and combine with Dampness, triggering an outbreak. Hot, humid weather mirrors the internal environment of Damp-Heat and can tip the balance. Cooling foods help clear Heat and drain Dampness, while gentle exercise moves Qi and prevents stagnation. Keeping the area clean and dry reduces external dampness, and stress reduction calms the Liver, preventing the surge of Heat downward.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat plenty of cooling, dampness-clearing foods like cucumber, celery, mung beans, and watermelon. Avoid spicy, greasy, or fried foods, as well as alcohol and coffee, which add Heat and Dampness. Keep the genital area clean and dry, wear loose cotton underwear, and manage emotional stress with gentle exercise like walking or yoga.

patterns.why_this_happens: When Damp-Heat lingers in the lower burner, it can intensify into Toxic-Heat, a more aggressive form of Heat that damages tissue and causes severe inflammation. The genital area becomes red, swollen, and extremely painful, with blisters that fill with thick yellow pus. Systemic symptoms like fever, chills, and intense thirst appear because the Toxin has spread beyond the local skin into the body's Qi level, overwhelming its defenses.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with prickly thorns, dry yellow coating. Pulse: rapid (shu) and forceful, often slippery (hua).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Toxic-Heat is a severe form of internal Heat that flares up when additional heat or stagnation is introduced. Spicy foods, alcohol, and emotional stress all generate more heat and fire, directly feeding the toxin. Cooling compresses, cold drinks, and rest help settle the uprising of Heat and allow the body's yin and defensive qi to regain control.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat cooling, hydrating foods like cucumber, watermelon, and mung beans. Avoid spicy, greasy, and fried foods that add internal heat. Keep the affected area clean and dry, and prioritize rest to allow the body's defenses to fight the toxin.

patterns.why_this_happens: When the body's cooling and moistening reserves (Yin) run low, a subtle but persistent heat rises from within. This empty heat has no dampness to bind it, so it flares upward and outward, irritating the delicate tissues of the genital area and causing recurrent, milder sores. Because the root is a deep deficiency, outbreaks tend to return whenever the body is stressed, overworked, or sleep-deprived - moments when Yin is further drained.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red, thin, dry body with cracks and little or no coating. Pulse: fine (thin) and rapid.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Yin deficiency means the body's cooling and moistening reserves are low. Late nights, overwork, and stress further deplete Yin, allowing empty heat to flare up and trigger genital sores. Spicy and drying foods add heat and consume fluids. Rest, hydration, and moistening foods replenish Yin, calming the empty heat and reducing outbreak frequency.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat moistening, cooling foods like pear, lily bulb, cucumber, and black sesame. Avoid spicy, fried, and drying foods. Prioritize rest, especially before midnight, and manage stress with gentle exercise like yoga or walking. Avoid excessive sexual activity that depletes Yin.

patterns.why_this_happens: When Qi and Blood are deficient, the tissues of the genital area lack proper nourishment and defense. The immune response is too weak to contain the virus, so outbreaks recur, but the body cannot mount a strong inflammatory reaction. This results in sores that are less red and painful, but they linger and heal very slowly, often flaring up after exhaustion or illness.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale body, may be thin or have teeth marks, with a thin white coating. Pulse: fine (thin) and weak, especially in the right Guan position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Qi and Blood are the foundation of the body's ability to heal and defend itself. Rest and nourishing foods replenish these resources, allowing the immune system to suppress the virus and repair damaged tissues. Overwork, poor diet, and stress drain Qi and Blood, leaving the genital area vulnerable to reactivation and making sores slow to heal.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat warm, cooked, nourishing foods such as soups, stews, and congees. Avoid raw, cold, and greasy foods that weaken the Spleen. Prioritize adequate sleep and gentle daily movement like walking or Qi Gong to build Qi without depleting it.

patterns.why_this_happens: When the body’s warming Yang Qi is weak, especially in the Kidneys and Spleen, Cold and Dampness can settle into the lower burner. Instead of the fiery, red, burning sores of heat patterns, this Cold-Damp congeals the flow of Qi and Blood in the genital area. The result is stubborn, hard, dark-colored sores that ooze thin fluid and ache dully, because the tissues are being starved of warmth and circulation rather than inflamed by heat.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale, swollen with teeth marks, thick white greasy coating, excessively moist. Pulse: deep, slow, and soggy, especially in the rear positions.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold and Dampness are the root of this pattern, causing the Qi and Blood to congeal into hard, painful sores. Cold environments and foods add more Cold, thickening the Dampness and worsening the ache. Warmth and drying measures do the opposite: they melt the Cold, dry up the Dampness, and get the Qi and Blood moving again, which softens the sores and eases the pain.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Keep the lower body warm and dry; avoid sitting on cold, damp surfaces. Favor warm, cooked foods like stews with ginger and cinnamon, and minimize raw, cold, or sweet foods that feed Dampness. Gentle movement, like walking, helps circulate Yang Qi without exhaustion.

It works by clearing the internal Heat driving the infection, improving local blood circulation to reduce swelling and pain, and helping the body expel pus and toxins. Historically called "the foremost formula in external medicine" and "the sacred remedy for abscesses," it is also applied in modern practice for conditions such as mastitis, inflammatory acne, tonsillitis, and appendicitis.

faqs.question: Can TCM cure genital herpes?
faqs.answer: TCM aims to strengthen your body so the virus stays dormant. While no treatment can eliminate the virus from your nerve cells, many patients find that outbreaks become much less frequent, milder, or even stop for years after addressing the underlying pattern. It's about managing the condition, not eradicating it.

faqs.question: Is acupuncture painful?
faqs.answer: Acupuncture needles are hair-thin and insertion is usually painless. For genital herpes, points are often on the legs, abdomen, or back, not directly on sores. Many people find sessions deeply relaxing.

faqs.question: Do I have to change my diet completely?
faqs.answer: You don't need a perfect diet, but certain foods can trigger outbreaks depending on your pattern. For example, if you have Damp-Heat, cutting back on spicy, greasy, and sugary foods helps. Your practitioner will give you specific guidance tailored to your pattern.

faqs.question: Can I use TCM alongside my antiviral medication?
faqs.answer: Yes, TCM and antivirals can be used together safely. Herbs and acupuncture may reduce the need for frequent medication over time, but never stop prescribed antivirals without consulting your doctor. Always inform both your TCM practitioner and your physician about everything you're taking.

faqs.question: Will the herbs have side effects?
faqs.answer: When prescribed correctly by a qualified practitioner, Chinese herbal formulas are generally well-tolerated. Any side effects are usually mild digestive adjustments. However, some herbs can interact with medications, so full disclosure is essential.

faqs.question: How soon will I see results?
faqs.answer: During an acute outbreak, many notice less pain and faster healing within a few days of starting herbs and acupuncture. For long-term prevention, it typically takes 4-8 weeks to see a clear reduction in outbreak frequency, though some patterns need longer.

faqs.question: Is TCM safe during pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Some acupuncture points and herbs are contraindicated in pregnancy. Always tell your practitioner if you are pregnant or trying to conceive. With proper adjustments, TCM can be used safely to manage outbreaks during pregnancy, but it must be done by a practitioner experienced in prenatal care.

research.title: Chinese herbal medicine for recurrent genital herpes: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials
research.description: This systematic review pooled data from multiple RCTs evaluating Chinese herbal formulas for recurrent genital herpes. The meta-analysis indicated that herbal medicine significantly reduced outbreak frequency and lesion healing time compared to placebo or conventional antivirals alone. However, the quality of included trials was generally low, with unclear randomization and blinding, highlighting the need for more rigorous research.
research.periodical: Liu J, et al. Chinese herbal medicine for recurrent genital herpes: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials. Complementary Therapies in Medicine. 2015;23(4):589-597.

research.title: Clinical observation on modified Longdan Xiegan Decoction in treating recurrent genital herpes
research.description: In this RCT, 80 patients with recurrent genital herpes were treated with a modified Longdan Xiegan Decoction or standard antiviral therapy. The herbal group showed a significant reduction in recurrence rate at 6-month follow-up and faster crusting of lesions. No serious adverse events were reported, suggesting good safety and tolerability.
research.periodical: Wang Y, Li X, Zhang H. Clinical observation on modified Longdan Xiegan Decoction in treating recurrent genital herpes. Chinese Journal of Integrated Traditional and Western Medicine. 2010;30(8):876-879.
